description: Cluster trust root. Three members co-sign this; only a root with three valid signatures from three distinct members it names itself authorises the operational key it binds. Canonical form and acceptance rules: contracts/consensus-protocol.md and identity-schema.json `cluster_trust_root`.
empty_by_default_rationale: There is no master until three nodes agree. A root with one or two signatures is not a partial success — it authorises nothing, so shipping this file empty means a fresh deployment has no master and no way to sign anything. That is the fail-closed default, same as the peer registry.
what_this_is_not: not a majority decision — three of three, deliberately
not threshold cryptography — three ordinary Ed25519 signatures over identical canonical bytes
not a configuration file — this is a signed agreement, and editing it invalidates all three signatures

root_template.nonce: UNIQUE_PER_ROOT — a re-formed root needs a new nonce so the previous one cannot be replayed

members.fingerprint: REPLACE — sha256 of the projected identity

root_template.master_node_id: REPLACE — must be one of the three members
root_template.master_pubkey: REPLACE — the operational public key this root authorises

signatures.REPLACE_node_id: REPLACE — all three, or the root authorises nothing

requires: exactly three members, all distinct node_ids
three signatures, from three distinct members the root itself names
each signature valid against that member's cluster_pubkey as stated in the root
master_node_id is one of the three members
a nonce not already in force, so a re-formed root supersedes rather than merges
verification.never_verified_here: Whether any root is actually valid on a live cluster. No three-node cluster exists on the development host.
